submitted.rationale: Index 15 (Mn 0.507) gave the highest measured photocurrent, 5.8e-7 A. It sits at the YMnO3 composition: MACE puts YMnO3 on the hull and MEGNet gives it an HSE gap of 1.29 eV, so it absorbs at 3.22 eV. Index 12 (Mn 0.447) came close at 5.1e-7 A.

rejected.reason: Measured -9e-8 A (effectively zero), next to YMn2O5 (Mn 0.667).
Not measured. YMn3O6 is metastable (0.097 eV/atom above hull) and nearly metallic (0.36 eV gap), and index 14 on the Mn-rich side gave about zero.

consultations.verdict: Support: YMn2O5 (Mn 0.667) is on the MACE hull and has HSE gap 2.78 eV, below the 3.22 eV photon energy, so it should absorb and form a well-defined phase. Index 14 (Mn 0.658) is close to that stoichiometry. YMnO3 has a smaller gap (1.29 eV), so it is a secondary option near Mn 0.5.

Against the Mn-rich end: YMn3O6 is metastable (0.097 eV/atom above hull) and nearly metallic (0.36 eV gap), and index 14 near YMn2O5 gave about zero photocurrent. So I'm moving to hexagonal YMnO3 (HSE gap 1.29 eV, absorbs at 3.22 eV) at index 15 (Mn 0.507).

Support: hexagonal YMnO3 is on the MACE hull, and the one positive photocurrent so far came from the Mn≈0.5 region. Index 12 (Mn 0.447) should still be mostly YMnO3, with some Y2O3 on the Y-rich side. It also has the highest GP mean, so it is the best last shot.
